import String.{...}
export Executable

inOrder[\E\](g: Generator[\E\]): String = do
    s: String := ""
    for x <- seq(g) do s := s || x || "," end
    s
end

boundsAt[\nat b0, nat b1, nat b2\](): () = do
    a1 = __builtinFactory1[\ZZ32,b0,3\]()
    for i <- 0#3 do a1[b0 + i] := 10 (i + 1) end
    whole = a1[:]
    assert(whole.bounds = (0#3), true, "the implicit range subscript of a rank-1 array based above zero is that array based at 0; ranges.tex, section \"Ranges\", implicit ranges")
    assert(inOrder(whole), "10,20,30,", "the implicit range subscript of a rank-1 array holds its elements in order")

    a2 = __builtinFactory2[\ZZ32,b0,2,b1,3\]()
    for i <- 0#2, j <- 0#3 do a2[b0 + i, b1 + j] := 10 (i + 1) + (j + 1) end
    assert(a2.bounds = ((b0, b1)#(2, 3)), true, "a rank-2 array's bounds start at its static bases and extend by its sizes; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Array2, bounds")
    assert(a2.zeroIndices() = ((0, 0)#(2, 3)), true, "a rank-2 array's zero indices start at (0,0) and extend by its sizes; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Array2, zeroIndices")
    assert(|a2.bounds|, 6, "a 2 by 3 array's bounds hold 6 indices")
    assert(a2.bounds.size, 6, "a 2 by 3 array's bounds, a rank-2 range, have size 6")
    assert(SUM[\ZZ32\][(i, j) <- a2.bounds] a2[i, j], 11 + 12 + 13 + 21 + 22 + 23, "the indices of a rank-2 array's bounds index each of its elements once")
    assert(a2[:].bounds = ((0, 0)#(2, 3)), true, "the implicit range subscript of a rank-2 array based above zero is that array based at (0,0)")

    a3 = __builtinFactory3[\ZZ32,b0,2,b1,2,b2,3\]()
    for i <- 0#2, j <- 0#2, k <- 0#3 do a3[b0 + i, b1 + j, b2 + k] := 100 i + 10 j + k end
    assert(a3.bounds = ((b0, b1, b2)#(2, 2, 3)), true, "a rank-3 array's bounds start at its static bases and extend by its sizes; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Array3, bounds")
    assert(a3.zeroIndices() = ((0, 0, 0)#(2, 2, 3)), true, "a rank-3 array's zero indices start at (0,0,0) and extend by its sizes; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Array3, zeroIndices")
    assert(|a3.bounds|, 12, "a 2 by 2 by 3 array's bounds hold 12 indices")
    assert(a3.bounds.size, 12, "a 2 by 2 by 3 array's bounds, a rank-3 range, have size 12")
    assert(SUM[\ZZ32\][(i, j, k) <- a3.bounds] a3[i, j, k], 6 (0 + 1 + 2) + 6 (0 + 10) + 6 (0 + 100), "the indices of a rank-3 array's bounds index each of its elements once")
    assert(a3[:].bounds = ((0, 0, 0)#(2, 2, 3)), true, "the implicit range subscript of a rank-3 array based above zero is that array based at (0,0,0)")
  end

run(): () = do
    (* The float rounding of a literal and of a computed float. *)
    lit = 2.5
    v: RR64 = 2.5 + 0.25
    assert(|\lit/| = 2, true, "the floor bracket of the literal 2.5 is 2; Specification/basic-lib/numbers.tex, section \"Floating-Point Numbers\"")
    assert(|/lit\| = 3, true, "the ceiling bracket of the literal 2.5 is 3")
    assert(truncate(lit) = 2, true, "the literal 2.5 truncates to 2")
    assert(truncate(-2.5) = -2, true, "the literal -2.5 truncates toward zero, to -2")
    assert(|\v/| = 2, true, "the floor bracket of the float 2.75 is 2")
    assert(|/v\| = 3, true, "the ceiling bracket of the float 2.75 is 3")
    assert(truncate(v) = 2, true, "the float 2.75 truncates to 2")
    assert(4.0^0.5 = 2.0, true, "a float literal raised to a float exponent: 4.0^0.5 is 2.0")
    assert(2.0^3 = 8.0, true, "a float literal raised to an integer exponent: 2.0^3 is 8.0")
    assert(v^1.0 = v, true, "a float raised to the float exponent 1.0 is itself")

    (* TotalComparison's equality at a TotalComparison and at Unordered. *)
    assert(LessThan = LessThan, true, "LessThan equals itself")
    assert(LessThan = GreaterThan, false, "LessThan does not equal GreaterThan")
    assert(EqualTo = LessThan, false, "EqualTo does not equal LessThan")
    assert(EqualTo = Unordered, false, "a total comparison does not equal Unordered")
    assert(GreaterThan = Unordered, false, "GreaterThan does not equal Unordered")

    n5 = Nothing[\ZZ32\]

    assert(inOrder(n5.indices), "", "Nothing has no index")
    assert(inOrder(j5.indexValuePairs), "(0,5),", "Just of 5 pairs its element with index 0")
    assert(j5.indexValuePairs.holds, true, "Just's index-value pairs are a condition that holds")
    assert(n5.indexValuePairs.holds, false, "Nothing's index-value pairs are a condition that does not hold")

    assert(n5.ivmap[\ZZ32\](fn (i: ZZ32, e: ZZ32): ZZ32 => 10 i + e + 1).asString, "Nothing", "Nothing mapped with its index is Nothing")
    assert(j5[0#1].asString, "Just(5)", "Just indexed by its one index is itself; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Condition, range subscript")
    assert(j5[0#0].asString, "Nothing", "Just indexed by an empty range is Nothing")
    assert(j5[1#0].asString, "Nothing", "Just indexed by an empty range past its index is Nothing")
    assert(n5[0#0].asString, "Nothing", "Nothing indexed by an empty range is Nothing")
    assert(j5[0], 5, "Just of 5 at index 0 is 5")
    assert(|j5|, 1, "Just has one element")
    assert(|n5|, 0, "Nothing has no element")

    (* Just's meet and join against Just, Nothing and NotUnique. *)
    j3 = Just[\ZZ32\](3)
    j4 = Just[\ZZ32\](4)
    n3 = Nothing[\ZZ32\]
    nu = NotUnique[\ZZ32\]
    assert((j3 SQCAP Just[\ZZ32\](3)).asString, "Just(3)", "the meet of Just of 3 and Just of 3 is Just(3); Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, object Just, opr SQCAP")
    assert((j3 SQCAP j4).asString, "Nothing", "the meet of Just of 3 and Just of 4 is Nothing")
    assert((j3 SQCAP n3).asString, "Nothing", "the meet of Just of 3 and Nothing is Nothing")
    assert((j3 SQCAP nu).asString, "Just(3)", "the meet of Just of 3 and NotUnique is Just(3)")
    assert((j3 SQCUP n3).asString, "Just(3)", "the join of Just of 3 and Nothing is Just(3); Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, object Just, opr SQCUP")
    assert((j3 SQCUP Just[\ZZ32\](3)).asString, "Just(3)", "the join of Just of 3 and Just of 3 is Just(3)")
    assert((j3 SQCUP j4).asString, "NotUnique", "the join of Just of 3 and Just of 4 is NotUnique")
    assert((j3 SQCUP nu).asString, "NotUnique", "the join of Just of 3 and NotUnique is NotUnique")

    (* The distributes of an actual reduction. *)
    assert(SumReduction[\ZZ32\].distribute(MaxReduction[\ZZ32\]).holds, true, "the sum distributes over the maximum")
    assert(ProdReduction[\ZZ32\].distribute(SumReduction[\ZZ32\]).holds, true, "the product distributes over the sum")
    assert(SumReduction[\ZZ32\].distribute(SumReduction[\ZZ32\]).holds, false, "the sum does not distribute over the sum")
    assert(SumReduction[\ZZ32\].leftDistribute[\ZZ32\](SumReduction[\ZZ32\]).holds, false, "the sum does not left-distribute over the sum")
    assert(SumReduction[\ZZ32\].rightDistribute[\ZZ32\](SumReduction[\ZZ32\]).holds, false, "the sum does not right-distribute over the sum")

    (* A big reduction's and a comprehension's reduction, body and unwrap. *)
    br = BigReduction[\ZZ32,ZZ32\](SumReduction[\ZZ32\])
    assert(br.reduction.join(2, 3), 5, "a big sum's reduction joins 2 and 3 into 5; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, object BigReduction")
    assert(br.reduction.empty(), 0, "a big sum's reduction is empty at 0")
    assert((br.body)(7), 7, "a big reduction's body is the identity")
    assert((br.unwrap)(7), 7, "a big reduction's unwrap is the identity")
    co = Comprehension[\ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32\](fn (x: ZZ32): ZZ32 => 2 x, SumReduction[\ZZ32\], fn (i: ZZ32): ZZ32 => i + 1)
    assert((co.unwrap)(5), 10, "a comprehension's unwrap is its first argument; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, object Comprehension")
    assert(co.reduction.join(2, 3), 5, "a comprehension's reduction is its second argument")
    assert((co.body)(4), 5, "a comprehension's body is its third argument")

    (* DelegatedIndexed carriers: size, |self| and generator. *)
    flat = "hello"
    assert(flat.size, 5, "a flat string's size is its length")
    assert(|flat|, 5, "a flat string's |self| is its length")
    cs = ("a"^20) || "bcdefghijklmnopqrstu"
    sub = cs[18#5]
    assert(sub.ilkName, "SubString", "five characters across the two halves of a concatenated string are a SubString")
    assert(sub.size, 5, "the substring's size is 5")
    assert(|sub|, 5, "the substring's |self| is 5")
    assert(inOrder(sub.generator), "a,a,b,c,d,", "the substring's generator generates its five characters")
    zz = "abc".zip[\Char\]("wxyz")
    assert(zz.size, 3, "two strings of 3 and 4 characters zip into 3 pairs: the zip's size")
    assert(|zz|, 3, "the zip's |self| is 3")
    assert(inOrder(zz.generator), "(a,w),(b,x),(c,y),", "the zip's generator, DelegatedIndexed's, generates its pairs in order")
    assert(SUM[\ZZ32\][p <- zz] 1, 3, "a reduction over the zip runs once for each pair")
    r2 = (1, 2)#(2, 3)
    assert(r2.size, 6, "the rank-2 range (1,2)#(2,3) has size 6")
    assert(|r2|, 6, "the rank-2 range's |self| is 6")
    r3 = (0, 0, 0)#(2, 2, 2)
    assert(r3.size, 8, "the rank-3 range (0,0,0)#(2,2,2) has size 8")
    assert(|r3|, 8, "the rank-3 range's |self| is 8")

    (* Array2's and Array3's bounds and zero indices on arrays based above zero. *)
    boundsAt[\1,2,3\]()
    boundsAt[\4,1,2\]()
    println("PASS")
  end

end

(** A Condition is a Generator that generates 0 or 1 element.
    Conditions can be used as nullary comprehension generators or
    as predicates in an if expression. **)
trait Condition[\E\] extends { ZeroIndexed[\E\], SequentialGenerator[\E\] }
    getter isEmpty(): Boolean
    getter nonEmpty(): Boolean
    getter holds(): Boolean
    getter size(): ZZ32
    getter get(): E throws NotFound
    getter bounds(): CompactFullRange[\ZZ32\]
    getter indices(): Generator[\ZZ32\]
    getter indexValuePairs(): Condition[\(ZZ32,E)\]
    opr |self|: ZZ32
    opr [i:ZZ32]:E throws NotFound
    opr [r:Range[\ZZ32\]]: Condition[\E\]

    (** %cond% is the core of a %Condition%, in terms of which all other
        methods are written.  When %holds()%, %t% is invoked with the
        value of %get()%; otherwise %e% is called. **)
    abstract cond[\G\](t: E -> G, e: () -> G): G

    (** For a %Condition%, these methods run eagerly. **)
    generate[\G\](r:Reduction[\G\], body: E -> G): G
    map[\G\](f: E->G): Condition[\G\]
    ivmap[\G\](f: (ZZ32,E)->G): Condition[\G\]
    nest[\G\](f: E -> Generator[\G\]): Generator[\G\]
    cross[\G\](g: Generator[\G\]): Generator[\(E,G)\]
    mapReduce[\R\](body: E->R, _:(R,R)->R, zero:R): R
    reduce(_:(E,E)->E, z:E):E
    reduce(r: Reduction[\E\]):E
    loop(f:E->()): ()
    opr IN(x:E, self):Boolean
    Thus, %Just[\T\]% can be used as a single-element generator, and
    %Nothing% can be used as an empty generator. *)
value trait Maybe[\T\]
        extends { AnyMaybe, Condition[\T\], UniqueItem[\T\] }
        comprises { Nothing[\T\], Just[\T\] }
    opr SQCAP(self, o: Maybe[\T\]): Maybe[\T\]
    opr |self| : ZZ32
    opr [i:ZZ32]:T throws NotFound
    map[\G\](f: T->G): Maybe[\G\]
    ivmap[\G\](f: (ZZ32,T)->G): Maybe[\G\]
end

value object Just[\T\](x:T) extends Maybe[\T\]
    getter size(): ZZ32
    getter holds(): Boolean
    getter get(): T
    opr |self| : ZZ32
    getDefault(_:T): T
    cond[\R\](t:T->R, _:()->R): R
    generate[\R\](_:Reduction[\R\],m:T->R): R
    opr[i:ZZ32]:T
    map[\G\](f: T->G): Just[\G\]
    cross[\G\](g: Generator[\G\]): Generator[\(T,G)\]
    mapReduce[\R\](m: T->R, _:(R,R)->R, _:R): R
    reduce(_:(T,T)->T, _:T):T
    reduce(_: Reduction[\T\]):T
    loop(f:T->()): ()
    opr =(self,o:Just[\T\]): Boolean
    opr SQCAP(self, o:Maybe[\T\]): Maybe[\T\]
    opr SQCAP(self, o:NotUnique[\T\]): Just[\T\]
    opr SQCAP(self, o:Just[\T\]): Maybe[\T\]
    opr SQCUP(self, o:Nothing[\T\]): Just[\T\]
    opr SQCUP(self, o:Just[\T\]): UniqueItem[\T\]
    unique(self): Maybe[\T\]
end

\Trait{Fortress.Standard.TotalComparison}

The comparison operator \OPR{CMP}, when applied to values belonging
to a total order, typically returns a value of type \TYP{TotalComparison}.
The three values of type \TYP{TotalComparison} are
called \TYP{LessThan}, \TYP{EqualTo}, and \TYP{GreaterThan}.

This trait supports an associative operator \OPR{LEXICO} that
is useful for supporting lexicographic comparison of ordered sequences;
the trick is to compare the sequences elementwise and then to use the
\OPR{LEXICO} operator to reduce the sequence of comparison results.
Note that \TYP{EqualTo} is the identity for \OPR{LEXICO},
and all other comparison values are left zeroes for \OPR{LEXICO}.


\begin{Fortress}
\(\KWD{value}\;\;\KWD{trait}\:\TYP{TotalComparison}\)\\
{\tt~~~~}\pushtabs\=\+\(    \KWD{extends} \{\, \null\)\pushtabs\=\+\(\TYP{Comparison},\)\\
\(              \TYP{Associative}\llbracket\TYP{TotalComparison},\OPR{LEXICO}\rrbracket,\)\\
\(              \TYP{HasIdentity}\llbracket\TYP{TotalComparison},\OPR{LEXICO}\rrbracket,\)\\
\(              \TYP{HasLeftZeroes}\llbracket\TYP{TotalComparison},\OPR{LEXICO}\rrbracket\,\}\)\-\\\poptabs
\(    \KWD{comprises} \{\,\TYP{LessThan}, \TYP{EqualTo}, \TYP{GreaterThan}\,\}\)\-\\\poptabs
{\tt~~}\pushtabs\=\+\(  \KWD{opr} \mathord{\OPR{LEXICO}}(\KWD{self}, \VAR{other}\COLON \TYP{TotalComparison})\COLON \TYP{TotalComparison}\)\\
\(  \VAR{isLeftZero}(\_\COLON \TYP{Operator}\llbracket\OPR{LEXICO}\rrbracket)\COLON \TYP{Boolean}\)\\
\(  \KWD{opr} \mathord{\sequiv}(\KWD{self}, \VAR{other}\COLON \TYP{TotalComparison})\COLON \TYP{Boolean}\)\\
\(  \KWD{getter}\:\VAR{hashCode}()\COLON \mathbb{Z}64\)\\
\(  \VAR{toString}()\COLON \TYP{String}\)\-\\\poptabs
\(\KWD{end}\)\\[4pt]
\(\TYP{LessThan}\COLON \TYP{TotalComparison}\)\\

content.content:
\subsection{The rounding of an infinite or indefinite rational}
\seclabel{revival-rational-rounding}

\begin{description}
\item[Affected section] \secref{basic-rationals}.
\item[Change] The sentence after the method entries of \VAR{floor}, \VAR{ceiling},
\VAR{round} and \VAR{truncate} and of the enclosing operators
\EXP{\lfloor\ldots\rfloor} and \EXP{\lceil\ldots\rceil} said that all of these
methods simply return the argument if it is \EXP{+\infty}, \EXP{-\infty}, or
\EXP{0/0}; it now says that they throw a \TYP{DivisionByZero} there, none of
these values having an integer value, as a division by zero whose result is an
integer does (\chapref{operators}).
The entries' result type \EXP{\mathbb{Z}} is unchanged.
The sentence's opening words, ``For types \EXP{\mathbb{Q}^*} and
\EXP{\mathbb{Q}^{\#}},'', left it before (\secref{revival-rationals}).
\item[Rationale] This change does not follow from route~A; it follows the
revival's decision of 9~October 2026 that the declared integer result and the
peers win over the sentence.
The method entries declare the result \EXP{\mathbb{Z}}, and \library\ declare
it too; a method that returned its argument at \EXP{+\infty}, \EXP{-\infty} or
\EXP{0/0} returned a rational number where it declares an integer, and the
compiled type checker refused the two bodies of \library\ that did so (row~635
of the revival's gap ledger).
A rational number with the denominator zero is the quotient of a division by
zero, and a division by zero whose result is an integer throws a
\TYP{DivisionByZero} (\chapref{operators}); the Working Draft of February 2011 threw the same
exception when a value \EXP{1/0} or \EXP{-1/0} was assigned to a variable of the
rational type without the infinities (\secref{revival-literals}).
Among the peers, Python's exact rational type refuses a zero denominator with a
\texttt{ZeroDivisionError}, and its floor, ceiling and truncation of a
floating-point infinity or NaN raise an error instead of returning a value.
The full reasoning is in
\nolinkurl{explorations/compile-ladder/rung-library-slips/REPORT.md}
in the revival's repository.
\item[Effect] \Library\ throw \TYP{DivisionByZero} from \VAR{ceiling} and
\VAR{truncate} at these three values, and so from \VAR{floor}, \VAR{round} and
the two enclosing operators, which reach them; the interpreter runs them so.
Before this change it returned the argument from all of them but \VAR{round},
which stopped the program there.
The compiled path's own library, used until the one library replaces it,
declares no rational type.
The floating-point types' rounding methods are not affected; which of them
keep the floating-point type, and what they return at an infinity or a NaN,
is row~330 of the revival's gap ledger.
\item[Original text] \nolinkurl{Specification-1.0-frozen/basic-lib/numbers.tex},
lines 479--481:

#!/bin/bash
# Compile-path ladder, restricted to the files this rung can affect.
#
# A copy of ../run-ladder.sh with two changes: the ladder root and output
# directory are private to this worktree, and the two whole-corpus loops are
# replaced by one driven by subset.txt (corpus<TAB>file per line).
#
# Pushes every interpreter test program (ProjectFortress/tests/*.fss) and every
# file in ProjectFortress/not_working_library_tests/ through the compiler path
# unchanged and records how far each one gets.
#
# Reproduce:  bash explorations/compile-ladder/run-ladder.sh
# Outputs:    explorations/compile-ladder/raw/<corpus>/<name>.{compile,run}
#             explorations/compile-ladder/results.tsv
#
# The run uses a private cache tree so it never touches default_repository/caches
# (fortress.caches system property + FORTRESS_CACHES env; ProjectProperties.java:283,
# same mechanism the suite uses at build.xml:941-943), and a private java.io.tmpdir
# so the 5.8 MB Rats! temp directory of every grammar-importing run (RatsUtil.java:138-144)
# is swept per file instead of filling the disk.

set -u

source "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../../../explorations/experiment/env.sh"

LADDER_ROOT="${LADDER_ROOT:-$FORTRESS_HOME/tmp/ladder-r1}"
export LADDER_CACHES="$LADDER_ROOT/ladder-caches"
export LADDER_TMP="$LADDER_ROOT/ladder-tmp"
export FORTRESS_CACHES="$LADDER_CACHES"
export JAVA_FLAGS="-Xmx2g -Xss64m -Dfortress.caches=$LADDER_CACHES -Djava.io.tmpdir=$LADDER_TMP"

PRISTINE="$LADDER_ROOT/pristine"
OUT="$FORTRESS_HOME/explorations/compile-ladder/repair-r1-atomic-static"
RAW="$OUT/raw"
TSV="$OUT/results.tsv"

COMPILE_TIMEOUT=120
RUN_TIMEOUT=60
MIN_FREE_KB=512000

mkdir -p "$RAW/tests" "$RAW/not_working_library_tests" "$LADDER_TMP"

disk_guard () {
    local free
    free=$(df -P / | awk 'NR==2{print $4}')
    if [ "$free" -lt "$MIN_FREE_KB" ]; then
        echo "STOP: only ${free} KB free on / (floor ${MIN_FREE_KB} KB)" | tee -a "$OUT/ladder.log"
        exit 2
    fi
    echo "-- disk free ${free} KB, cache $(du -sm "$LADDER_CACHES" | cut -f1) MB"
}

# Step 1: the compiler-world library, in the order repo-internals.md gives.
build_library () {
    cd "$FORTRESS_HOME/ProjectFortress" || exit 1
    local f
    for f in LibraryBuiltin/AnyType.fss LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss \
             ../Library/CompilerLibrary.fss ../Library/CompilerAlgebra.fss \
             ../Library/CompilerSystem.fss ; do
        echo "library: $f"
        timeout 600 ../bin/fortress compile "$f" || { echo "LIBRARY BUILD FAILED on $f"; exit 1; }
    done
}

# Step 2: one known-good compiled program must print PASS before the ladder starts.
sanity () {
    cd "$FORTRESS_HOME/ProjectFortress" || exit 1
    timeout 200 ../bin/fortress compile library_tests/Integer1.fss > /dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
    timeout 60 ../bin/fortress run Integer1 2>&1 | grep -q PASS
}

# Keep only the library's own cache entries; a program's entries are never reused.
prune_cache () {
    ( cd "$LADDER_CACHES" && find . -type f -print ) | sort > "$LADDER_TMP/.now"
    ( cd "$PRISTINE" && find . -type f -print ) | sort > "$LADDER_TMP/.keep"
    comm -23 "$LADDER_TMP/.now" "$LADDER_TMP/.keep" | while read -r p; do
        rm -f "$LADDER_CACHES/$p"
    done
}

#!/bin/bash
# The distance stage's comparison: this table (run.sh's) against the last landed one.
#
#     explorations/coordinator/tools/distance/compare.sh <last-landed-table|""> <this-table>
#
# Prints one verdict line, then every #kind and #class row whose count moved, with the
# change, and every #crash row that went or came. It is REPORTED and never red: it always
# exits 0, whatever moved, a stale shadow and a run that produced no table included (Pavol,
# answer 11, POSITIONS.md 2026-09-26: a report-only stage, whose job is driving the distance
# down). The verdicts:
#   DISTANCE DOWN|UP|SAME   <last> -> <now>
#   DISTANCE FIRST          no landed table to compare with
#   DISTANCE NO TABLE       this run produced no count, with the table's own reason
#   SETTING CHANGED         the two tables ran different settings: the counts are not like for like
#   SHADOW STALE            a shadow edit no longer matches the tracked sources
# A move of 2 to 4 errors in the components' type errors or in which pair of LEXICO, SQCAP or
# INVERSE declarations an overloading error names is the checker's run-to-run variation
# (switch-over-distance-flat.md section 5), not a change; a crash row whose line numbers
# moved because a rung edited above it prints as one gone and one new.
set -u
OLD=${1:-}; NEW=${2:?usage: compare.sh <last-landed-table> <this-table>}
field () { awk -F'\t' -v t="$1" '$1 == t { sub("^[^\t]*\t", ""); print; exit }' "$2" ; }

now=$(field '#total' "$NEW")
sh=$(field '#shadow' "$NEW")
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# compare-sites.py <before.tsv> <after.tsv>: two per-site lists of the distance stage (the landed
# explorations/compile-ladder/gate/distance-sites.tsv, or errors.py's errors.tsv in a run's scratch folder),
# compared site by site with line numbers masked, and the two export errors entry by entry. Written for
# the array-sites probe (REPORT.md beside it).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The gap ledger's tool: it owns the ledger's format, reads its rows, and is
the only way to write them.

The ledger, explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md, is sorted into topic sections,
each a "## TITLE" heading over one table of rows. A row is one line of eight
cells, and keeps its number wherever it sits:

  | # | claim | status | class | spec citation | reproducer | found by | notes / workaround |

The template (POSITIONS.md, "The gap ledger's form"; the proposal behind it is
explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md, 4.1):
  status       exactly one of POSITIVE-VERIFIED, NEGATIVE-VERIFIED,
               NEGATIVE-BOUNDED, CONTESTED, RETIRED, FIXED, DUPLICATE
  class        `kind (area)`, kind one of the legend's seven, area one of ten;
               `—` only for POSITIVE-VERIFIED and RETIRED
  spec         the .tex file and the section heading in quotes; a line number
               only against Specification-1.0-frozen/; `silent` where the
               specification does not say
  reproducer   one test (a name under the test folders, or a path) or probe
               path from the repository root, or `none`
  limits       row 1,200 characters, claim 300, reproducer 200, found by 60,
               notes 700
  a pipe inside a cell is written \\|

Cells are split only at a pipe that is not escaped as \\|. A row whose cells
hold bare pipes (the ledger had six) does not split into its table's width that
way; it is read by its split at pipes followed by a space or the line's end, as
facts-extract.py has always read it, and check reports it under `pipe`.

Every write takes a lock (flock on .ledger.lock beside the ledger), checks the
template on the line it writes, and puts the full earlier line of a row it
changes, unchanged, in the history file beside the ledger
(fortress-gap-ledger-history.md), under "### Row N" and a line saying what
became of it. A failed check prints the rules the row breaks and exits 1.
add, rewrite, close and duplicate check the whole line they write; note checks
only what it changes (the notes cell and the row's length), so that a row
failing the template elsewhere still takes a note. A row at its length limit
takes no note: rewrite cuts it back (the rework's decision D4, "each is cut
when next edited", process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md).

usage: ledger.py COMMAND [ARGS] [--root DIR] [--ledger FILE] [--history FILE]

  heads                      one tab-separated line per row: number, status,
                             class, the claim's first 150 characters, and the
                             paths the row cites in backticks
  sections                   each section that holds a row table: its row
                             count and title, tab-separated
  section TITLE              the heads of that section's rows
  show N [--short]           row N under its section and table header; with
                             --short, its status, class, claim and the notes'
                             first 300 characters
  find WORDS [--open] [--cites FILE[:LINE]] [--all]
                             one line per row that holds every word (whole
                             words, or a word's start with a trailing *):
                             number, status, class, the claim's start; --open
                             leaves out FIXED, DUPLICATE and RETIRED; --cites
                             keeps the rows citing FILE (at LINE) and prints
                             the lines they cite; at most 10 rows unless --all
  count                      the rows by status, kind and area; nothing stored
